text:
maria: heads up - saw a p99 tail blowout on prod around 18:05 UTC. correlated with a handful of long prompts + nested tool calls from a single tenant. p95 fine, p99 ~3x usual. :grimacing:
raj: ugh. any obvious kernel/quantization mismatches?
kai: initial traces show kernel fallback on last-token attention path. lots of small microbatches suddenly merged -> kv cache churn.
maria: exact symptoms: single requests with ~8k+ input tokens, then generator that calls tools repeatedly (10-20 tool calls). we hit dynamic batching that assumed short context.
oliver: do we have profiler output? flamegraph or top stacks would help.
maria: pasted minimal profiler dump below (trimmed):
```
2028-11-03T18:05:12Z profiler: request_id=abc123
- tokenize (50ms)
- initial forward (120ms) -> kernel: fast-attn-f32
- seq>2048 branching -> kernel fallback: long-attn-ref (980ms)
- kv-warmup (cache invalidate) (40ms)
- tool-call loop: 12 iterations (avg 150ms each, but spikes to 900ms on iteration 9)
- final decode (130ms)
total: ~3.8s (p99)
```
raj: hmm fallback to long-attn-ref is our big offender. why did kernel picker choose that? should've used chunked-optimized kernel for this model.
kai: kernel picker has heuristics based on seq_len histogram & batch shape. because microbatching collapsed many in-flight short requests into one batch with outlier long request, we ended up feeding a mixed-shape batch that tripped the fallback.
maria: also noticed KV eviction messages right before the slow kernel: `kv_cache: evict shard=7 reason=shape-mismatch`
oliver: eviction -> cache miss -> recompute keys for many layers -> longer path. that explains tool-call iteration spike when the tool call forced context switches.
raj: can we reproduce in staging with a synthetic generator that alternates long prompt + many tool calls?
kai: yes. i'm running a repro job now. initial idea: tighten microbatch heuristics to avoid merging long-context requests with short ones. two paths: 1) pre-classify by estimated seq_len and route to separate batch pool; 2) enforce max_batch_size_for_long_seq=1 so long jobs run isolated.
maria: both sound reasonable. tradeoffs: isolation reduces throughput and increases cost, but should reduce tail-latency. need a policy toggle per-tenant.
oliver: another mitigation: kernel override for known model family when seq_len>2048 -> force chunked-optimized kernel even if shapes mixed. downside: the chunked kernel has slightly higher overhead for pure-long-only batches? check perf regression.
kai: confirmed: chunked-optimized shows 10% higher per-token latency for pure-long sequences but 6x lower for mixed batches vs fallback. net win for our outlier case.
perf-bot: experiment scheduled: kernel-override + separate-queue policy on staging (job id: exp_20281103_09).
maria: good. also let's add a fast KV warmup path: when request includes tool calls, prefetch keys for first N layers while waiting for tool response (non-blocking). idea: amortize KV regen during external IO.
raj: neat. that should hide some of the recompute cost. but be careful with memory pressure if we prefetch too aggressively. add heuristics: prefetch only when estimated tool-call count > 2 and estimated seq_len > 1024.
kai: adding config snippet i'm testing:
```yaml
microbatch:
  split_by_estimated_len: true
  long_seq_threshold: 2048
  max_batch_for_long_seq: 1
  kernel_override:
    enable: true
    model_families: ["mistral-7b","rwkv-11b"]
kv:
  prefetch_on_tool: true
  prefetch_layers: 6
  prefetch_condition:
    min_tool_calls: 2
    min_seq_len: 1024
```
maria: looks good. timeline? can we validate on staging and run A/B that checks p99 and throughput delta?
kai: running smoke now. initial staging run shows p99 drop from 3.4s -> 1.1s for the repro, throughput drop ~8% for long<->short mixed synthetic traffic.
oliver: 8% is acceptable if we get 3x p99 improvement. capture token-cost delta.
raj: add alert rule: if kernel_override triggers > 5% of requests for a tenant for >10m, flag for review (cost impact).
maria: also add a lightweight profiler event when kv_eviction happens referencing request_id so we can correlate quickly in the future.
kai: done. one more thought: tool-calling loops sometimes amplify generation length unpredictably. add safety cap on tool loop depth and token budget per-request at the router (configurable per tenant).
maria: agreed. add default cap 12 tool calls / 4k generated tokens. exceptions via tenant policy.
oliver: ok let's ship the staging patch (kernel override + microbatch split + kv prefetch) behind a feature flag and run perf-bot experiment.
perf-bot: experiment started: exp_20281103_09 -> routing=split+override, kv_prefetch=true. collecting p95/p99/throughput for 2h.
maria: thanks team. follow up in morning with results. :thumbsup:
